He reported cramps of the abdominal muscles which occurred sporadically when in a supine position, but was otherwise without complaints. On neurological examination there was persistent bilateral mild ptosis and bilaterally positive Babinski sign, but no other abnormal findings. EMG of axial muscles did not show any pathological spontaneous activity. However, PET-CT revealed increased metabolism in several enlarged mediastinal as well as left-sided supraclavicular lymph nodes ( Fig. 1 b, c, d). Histological and immunohistochemical evaluation of bioptic specimens established a diagnosis of nodular sclerosing HL. A total of four cycles of polychemotherapy were performed according to the ABVD protocol (doxorubicin, bleomycin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine). Follow-up PET-CT four months after the first cycle revealed a significant reduction of the previously enlarged and hypermetabolic lymph nodes, indicating a good treatment response. Another two months later, no pathological PET activity was detectable. During chemotherapy, the neurological status of the patient showed progressive further improvement. There were no more cramps of axial muscles or startle responses, the pruritus subsided and the medication with benzodiazepines and tiagabine could be tapered off completely. The patient was able to return to school and had no limitations in his daily life. Fourteen months after diagnosis of HL he returned to the hospital for a follow-up evaluation which showed a normal neurological examination, with only minimal residual bilateral ptosis.
